rules.when: Hard or high-stakes Krunchix customer mobile-app work: architecture, a novel or ambiguous UI/UX flow, design-system decisions, cross-screen navigation or offline behaviour, a risky multi-file feature/refactor, release/store work, or a bug whose cause is not clear. This is the Expo/React Native app under frontend/apps/mobile in the Krunchix/krunchix monorepo, including shared packages when the change is for the app. Excludes image generation and fresh-news research requiring their dedicated tool-specific rules.
rules.why: Captain ladder (2026-09-27): Claude through the claude CLI first, then the ChatGPT pool through Pi. Claude never runs through Pi (Pi bills Claude as extra usage) and Cursor is retired. Exceptional work is architecture and brainstorming: Fable 5.1 xhigh, falling back to GPT-6 Astra xhigh, which matches Fable's Artificial Analysis index (53) at about 40% of its cost per task. Difficult work is complex coding: Opus 5.5 (the `opus` alias from Claude Code 2.1.280) leads Terminal-Bench 4.0 (66.4) and CursorBench 4.0 (57.8) over Fable, and GPT-6 Astra high is its closest Codex match (57.9 Terminal-Bench). Routine work: Sonnet 5, falling back to GPT-6 Sol ($2/$10). The 15% Codex floor keeps a reserve for the coordinator, which also runs on Codex. Report actual runtime errors before any fallback; authentication and network failures are not proof of exhausted quota. Never downgrade capability merely for quota.

rules.when: Well-specified, bounded Krunchix customer mobile-app work: a localized bug with a known cause, an existing-design UI implementation, a focused screen/component change, a targeted test, or documentation. Escalate to the hard mobile-app rule when the task becomes ambiguous, cross-cutting, or visually novel. Excludes image generation and fresh-news research requiring their dedicated tool-specific rules.
rules.why: Mobile implementation follows the same claude CLI -> Codex ladder as the hard mobile rule. Bounded work runs on Sonnet 5 and falls back to GPT-6 Sol, the value tier of GPT-6 (about a fifth of Astra's price per token). Jev uncertainty requires intake clarification, not an invented model choice.

rules.when: Outside the Krunchix customer mobile app (which uses its dedicated mobile rules), the task is architecture, technical or product design, research, investigation, planning, a scout report, an audit, or any work that is genuinely open-ended and needs deep reasoning before code.
rules.why: Captain's standing rule: Fable 5.1 for architecture, research and brainstorming, with GPT-6 Astra xhigh as its Codex counterpart.

rules.when: The task depends on fresh news, current events, live public facts, or recent market, library, or product changes where up-to-the-minute web context is central.
rules.why: Web research is search and reading heavy rather than reasoning heavy. Claude Code has native web search; Pi has pi-web-access.

rules.when: The task requires GENERATING IMAGES: creating, rendering, or producing image files such as icons, illustrations, marketing assets, or app store artwork.
rules.why: Only the OpenAI models generate images, and image generation is a Codex CLI tool rather than a Pi one, so this is the single rule that keeps the codex harness.

rules.when: The task is a big or ambiguous multi-file feature, a risky refactor, or work that requires holding many moving parts in mind, outside the mobile app. In the Odoo repo: a new module, a new model with its access rules, views and data, a change spanning several modules, a data migration, or POS/JS work.
rules.why: Complex coding: Opus 5.5 first, GPT-6 Astra high as its closest Codex match.

rules.when: The task is a simple bug fix whose root cause and fix are already clear, a small well-defined change, a test addition, or a documentation update. In the Odoo repo: a change inside one existing module such as a new field, a compute, a view tweak, a cron, a report column, or a test.
rules.why: Well-defined work: Sonnet 5, falling back to GPT-6 Sol.

rules.when: The task is to validate an already-defined change or PR: run the deterministic local checks, run the Jev quick check against the task spec, inspect GitHub CI, and report the result. Escalate a product or design decision rather than spending a premium model deciding it.
rules.why: Validation is command, test, lint and CI heavy rather than a primary design task. There is no no-mistakes pipeline; correctness and complexity come from Jev plus the deterministic checks.

rules.when: The task is a trivial mechanical edit such as a rote rename, formatting sweep, targeted typo fix, dependency bump with green CI, or simple file gathering.
rules.why: Cheapest fast profile when the task is narrow and low ambiguity. GPT-6 Luna is the Haiku-class Codex tier.
